gotchas.text: Prefix caching defaults OFF for hybrid-attention models (is_hybrid=True), even though it is on by default for everything else in vLLM V1. Pass --enable-prefix-caching explicitly or you will silently benchmark an uncached engine.
--reasoning-parser qwen3 resolves but qwen3_xml does not; --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml resolves but qwen3 does not. The two flags take different names for the same model.
Thinking is on by default at reasoning_effort xhigh, which produced a single 63-minute response. Cap the effort or the output tokens before running anything timed.

MTP draft acceptance by position was 82 % / 66 % / 48 %, a mean of 2.96 tokens per forward pass. That multiplier is what lets 16.5 tok/s beat the 9.6 tok/s the memory bandwidth would otherwise allow for 28.5 GB of weights at 273 GB/s.

provenance.notes: Single-stream decode with MTP-3: 18.9 tok/s on code, 14.1 tok/s on prose; decode_tok_s_per_request.mean is the midpoint of the two, with the two ends recorded as min and max. vram_peak_gb is the 50.3 GiB engine footprint at a 256K context, converted to GB. KV cache held 271,315 tokens with prefix caching (348,497 without) at 0.44 gpu-memory-utilization. Prefix caching also turned a 19K-token shared prefix prefill from 12.64 s into 0.89 s, and a 53K prefix from 26.62 s into 1.21 s. An embedding engine (Qwen3-Embedding-8B, about 10 GiB) was resident alongside vLLM during these measurements; the box was otherwise idle. started_at carries the date the measurement was taken; the clock time is a placeholder because only the date was written down. Measured by hand on the author's own machine before the harness existed, then mapped onto this workload because it matches what was run. It is not an atlas-bench run: re-running it with the harness is a wanted reproduction, not a duplicate.
